title.narrative: Mozambique Safer Roads for Socio-Economic Integration Program

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective is to improve road connectivity, safety, and climate resilience and develop social inclusion in the Project areas.

The development objective of Safer Roads for Socio-Economic Integration Program Project for Mozambique is to improve road connectivity, safety, and climate resilience in the Program areas. This project has five components. 1) The first component, Safe and Resilient Road Connectivity, aims to focus on safe and climate resilient rehabilitation, improvement, and maintenance of the most critical and climate vulnerable sections of the N1 corridor through Output- and performance-based road contracts (OPBRC). 2) The second component, Community Engagement and Women Empowerment, will explore ways to focus on women not as SEA/SH survivors, but as productive community members with voice and agency, and create jobs for women through multiple community-based pilots in the roads sector. 3) The third component, Improved Road Safety Management, will finance necessary technical assistance to help the government achieve SDG 3.6 (decrease the number of road crash fatalities by 50 percent by 2030). 4) The fourth component, Institutional Development and Project Management, aims to finance institutional development, capacity building, and project management costs. 5) The fifth component, Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC), aims to facilitate access to rapid financing by allowing uncommitted project funds to be reallocated in the event of a natural disaster upon formal declaration of a national or regional state of emergency and a formal request from the government.

condition.narrative: Section I.A.2 of Schedule 2: The Recipient, not later than 30 days after the Effective Date shall appoint and shall cause RF toappoint (through the ANE Cooperation Agreement) and thereafter maintain throughout Project implementation, a Project coordinator(for the MTC-PIU); and a Project coordinator, an environmental specialist, a social/resettlement specialist, a GBV/SEA/SH expert; asenior highway engineer, a road safety expert, and a drainage/bridges engineer (for the ANE-PIU).

Section I.A.3 (a) of Schedule 2: The Recipient shall appoint for the PIU-MTC, not later than 120 days after the Effective Date, andthereafter maintain throughout Project implementation, a senior road safety specialist (policy), a senior road safety specialist(data management), an assistant accountant, a procurement specialist and a database specialists (safety).

Section I.A.3 (b) of Schedule 2: The Recipient shall cause RF to appoint, for the ANE-PIU (through the ANE Cooperation Agreement),not later than 120 days after the Effective Date, and thereafter maintain throughout Project implementation, a road safetyspecialist (shared with the PIU-MTC), an engineer, a procurement specialist, and a monitoring and evaluation specialist.

Section I.A.3 (c) of Schedule 2: The Recipient shall cause RF to appoint (through the ANE Cooperation Agreement) for the provincialdelegations of ANE-PIU located in the provinces of Cabo Delgado, Sofala, and Zambezia, not later than 120 days after the EffectiveDate, and thereafter maintain throughout Project implementation, three (3) environmental specialists; three (3) social/resettlementspecialists; three (3) GBV/SEA/SH experts; and three (3) occupational health and safety (OHS) officers, one in each province, allrecruited on the basis of terms of reference, qualifications, and experience acceptable to the Association.

Section I.A.4 of Schedule 2: The Recipient shall establish, not later than four (4) months after the Effective Date, and maintain,throughout the implementation of the Project, a steering committee (“Project Steering Committee” or “PSC”), with a composition,mandate, and resources satisfactory to the Association and detailed in the POM.

Section I.A.6 (i) of Schedule 2:The Recipient shall and shall cause RF to, not later than 120 days after the Effective Date hire,and thereafter maintain throughout Project implementation, a third-party monitoring agency, under terms of reference and withqualifications and experience satisfactory to the Association, to carry out an independent review of the Project's implementationand verification of results, including adherence to all aspects of the POM and ESCP, and an independent assessment of the Project'scompliance with the ESF instruments, with a particular focus on GBV/SEA/SH aspects.

Section I.A.6 (ii) of Schedule 2:The Recipient shall and shall cause RF to, not later than 120 days after the Effective Date hire,and thereafter maintain throughout Project implementation, a third-party monitoring provider for SEA/SH, under terms of referenceand with qualifications and experience satisfactory to the Association, to monitor the actions related to the implementation of theGVB risk management outlined in the SEA/GBV/SH Risk Assessment and Action Plan.

Section I.D.1 of Schedule 2: The Recipient shall and shall cause RF and ANE (through the Cooperation Agreement among MTC, RF andANE), not later than thirty (30) days after the Effective Date, to carry out the Project in accordance with the Project OperationalManual (“POM”), acceptable to the Association.

Section I.E (a) of Schedule 2:The Recipient shall and shall cause RF to carry out jointly with the Association, not later than June1, 2025, or such other period as may be agreed with the Association, a midterm review to assess the status of Projectimplementation, including as measured against the indicators referred to in Section 5.08(a) of the General Conditions.

Section I.E (b) of Schedule 2: The Recipient shall and shall cause RF to prepare and furnish to the Association, not later than one(1) month before the mid term review, a report, in scope and detail satisfactory to the Association and integrating the results ofthe monitoring and evaluation activities performed pursuant to Section 5.08(a) of the General Conditions, on the progress achievedin the carrying out of the Project during the period preceding the date of such report and setting out the measures recommended toensure the efficient carrying out of the Project and the achievement of the objective thereof during the period following suchdate.

Section I.H of Schedule 2: For the purposes of implementing Part 4(a)(vi) of the Project, the Recipient shall, not later than June1, 2025, or any other date acceptable to the Association, develop a comprehensive tolling strategy for the Recipient's primarynetwork, examining technical and economic viability as well as distributional impacts of road pricing and strategies to minimizeand mitigate any negative social outcomes, all in a manner acceptable to the Association.

Section I.I of Schedule 2: The Recipient, not later than 30 days after the Effective Date shall, and shall cause RF and ANE(through the ANE Cooperation Agreement), to submit a Project-level procurement strategy for development (“PPSD”), in form andsubstance acceptable to the Association, for the design of the appropriate procurement arrangements and packaging to achieve valuefor money and fit for purpose.
